native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: In the 17th century BCE (bin starting 1700 BCE; 1700–1601 BCE), the diversity of pottery form collapsed (Z: +0.74 → −1.13, ΔZ = −1.87, the largest negative form-slope in the 4300–500 BCE record) while the diversity of pottery decoration simultaneously increased (Z: −0.48 → +0.97, ΔZ = +1.45, a top-percentile positive decoration-slope), and this anti-phase transition is the only century in the entire record where both conditions coincide in the same 100-year bin under empirically fixed 5%/95% slope thresholds; the new regime then persisted for ~10 centuries (form flat at −1.13, decoration at +0.97/+1.53).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded capital.csv (decimal=','), mapped BCE→CE=-BCE and verified numeric identity with time_series_data.csv raw PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration on all 37 overlapping century bins (max diff 0.0). 2) Computed century-to-century slopes dZ (newer minus older) on the raw 100-yr values (primary). 3) Fixed collapse/increase thresholds as the 5th/95th percentiles of the empirical slope distributions before inspecting any result. 4) Detected bins satisfying both conditions in the same century (unique: 1700 BCE) plus ±100-yr sensitivity and 100-yr-rolling-mean confirmation on the annual _inter series (both criteria also met; Spearman corr of slopes ~0.57–0.58). 5) Exported full evidence table (slope_evidence_table.csv) and the executed script (analysis_pottery.py).

sub_hypo.relations: Pottery Form diversity collapses while Pottery Decoration diversity increases.

sub_hypo.text: In the 17th century BCE, pottery-form diversity collapsed from Z = +0.74 to −1.13, a change of −1.87 and the largest negative century-to-century form slope in the 4300–500 BCE record.
sub_hypo.context: The 1700–1601 BCE bin, starting at 1700 BCE, compared with the full 4300–500 BCE archaeological record using raw 100-year values.
sub_hypo.relations: Pottery-form diversity decreased by ΔZ = −1.87 (newer minus older), the record's largest negative form slope, meeting the empirically fixed 5th-percentile collapse threshold.

sub_hypo.text: In the same 17th-century BCE bin, pottery-decoration diversity increased from Z = −0.48 to +0.97, a change of +1.45 and a top-percentile positive decoration slope.
sub_hypo.context: The 1700–1601 BCE bin within the 4300–500 BCE archaeological record, using raw 100-year values.
sub_hypo.relations: Pottery-decoration diversity increased by ΔZ = +1.45 (newer minus older), meeting the empirically fixed 95th-percentile increase threshold.

sub_hypo.text: The bin starting at 1700 BCE is the only century in the 4300–500 BCE record where pottery-form collapse and pottery-decoration increase simultaneously meet the empirically fixed 5th/95th-percentile slope thresholds.
sub_hypo.context: All 100-year bins in the 4300–500 BCE archaeological record; thresholds fixed from empirical century-to-century slope distributions before inspecting results, with ±100-year sensitivity checks and 100-year-rolling-mean confirmation on annual interpolated series.
sub_hypo.relations: A unique simultaneous anti-phase transition: form slope meets the 5th-percentile collapse threshold while decoration slope meets the 95th-percentile increase threshold in the same bin. Both criteria also hold in the workflow's sensitivity and rolling-mean confirmation.

sub_hypo.text: Following the 17th-century BCE transition, the new pottery-diversity regime persisted for approximately ten centuries, with form diversity flat at Z = −1.13 and decoration diversity at Z = +0.97/+1.53.
sub_hypo.context: Approximately ten centuries following the 1700–1601 BCE transition in the archaeological record.
sub_hypo.relations: Persistent contrasting levels over time: pottery-form diversity remained flat at −1.13 while pottery-decoration diversity remained at +0.97/+1.53.
